newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HBG says UK, German markets remain tough.
newsitem.headline: HBG says UK, German markets remain tough.

text.p: Hollandsche Beton Groep NV said a relatively buoyant construction market in the Netherlands had helped offset less favourable conditions in Britain and Germany.

"The developments in the construction market in the United Kingdom and in Germany remain not so favourable. In the Netherlands and in the other countries where HBG is active, developments are better. The world dredging market remains good," it said in a statement with its first-half 1996 results.

HBG said first-half turnover had risen four percent to 2.71 billion guilders despite a long period of freezing weather in northwest Europe at the beginning of the year. The group's order book rose by 13 percent to 5.20 billion guilders.
First-half net profit from ordinary operations rose to 57 million guilders from 40 million.

Net profit including extraordinary items fell to 53 million guilders from 55 million because this year's first-half results included an extraordinary charge of four million guilders versus a gain of 15 million in the first half of 1995.
